stories.headline: Pentagon confirms 5,000-troop withdrawal from Germany as Trump-Merz rift deepens over Iran war
stories.summary: The US Pentagon formally announced the withdrawal of approximately 5,000 troops from Germany over the next 6–12 months, fulfilling Trump's threat after Chancellor Merz publicly accused the US of lacking a strategy in the Iran war and said Iran was 'humiliating' Washington. Trump subsequently threatened further withdrawals, cancelled a Biden-era plan to deploy Tomahawk missiles to Germany, and attacked Merz personally on Truth Social. Senior Republican congressional leaders Wicker and Rogers broke with the administration to warn the move undermined NATO deterrence and sent the wrong signal to Russia. NATO said it was seeking clarification. Defense Minister Pistorius called the withdrawal 'foreseeable' and urged European allies to assume greater responsibility; Foreign Minister Wadephul described the transatlantic alliance as 'robust' and downplayed the significance of the withdrawal.

stories.headline: Merz marks one year as chancellor with tense TV appearance, warning SPD against complacency in coalition
stories.summary: On the eve of the one-year anniversary of his chancellorship, Chancellor Merz appeared on the ARD talk show 'Caren Miosga' where he delivered an unusually sharp warning to coalition partner SPD, saying 'there is no left-wing majority in Germany' and demanding reciprocal compromise. He also rejected Klingbeil's plan to raise taxes on top earners ('not with me'), addressed the US troop withdrawal as 'nothing new,' and was asked about Timmy the whale. Media coverage extensively analysed his communication style, with surveys showing 58% of Germans expect the coalition to collapse before its term ends.

stories.headline: Klingbeil pushes income tax reform targeting top earners, presents 2027 budget framework
stories.summary: Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil announced plans to present an income tax reform concept 'in coming weeks' that would relieve 95% of workers while raising taxes on those earning six-figure salaries. The same week he presented the 2027 budget framework (Eckwerte) featuring record investment levels of €118bn but also requiring 1% spending cuts from most ministries. Chancellor Merz publicly rejected the top-earner tax element ('not with me'), creating an intra-coalition flashpoint.

stories.headline: Foreign Minister Wadephul calls Iranian counterpart, demands immediate opening of Strait of Hormuz and nuclear weapons renunciation
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul telephoned his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi and demanded the immediate opening of the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's 'complete and verifiable' renunciation of nuclear weapons, stating Germany shared the same goal as the US as a 'close ally.' The call came amid ceasefire negotiations in the US-Israel-Iran war; Iran and the US simultaneously threatened to resume hostilities, while Iran presented a 14-point peace plan.

stories.headline: Foreign Minister Wadephul visits Morocco for strategic dialogue, calls for more skilled workers and renewable energy cooperation
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Wadephul made a two-day visit to Rabat for the German-Moroccan strategic dialogue, meeting his counterpart Bourita, advocating for expanded skilled-worker migration, renewable energy cooperation, and stronger bilateral ties. He also played football with a youth women's team and telephoned US Secretary of State Rubio on the sidelines to discuss the Iran war. The visit was overshadowed by the breaking Trump-Merz row.

stories.headline: Bundeswehr expansion and modernisation: procurement, drones, wehrpflicht letters, and new strategic posture
stories.summary: Multiple overlapping stories about the Bundeswehr's ongoing expansion this week: Rheinmetall received a €1bn+ order for soldier systems (IdZ-ES); the Bundeswehr sent questionnaires to nearly 200,000 eighteen-year-olds under the new military service modernisation law; the army reclaimed former navy land in Kiel; Chancellor Merz visited exercises in Munster to observe drone warfare demonstrations; and Defence Minister Pistorius presented a new strategic document describing Russia as adversary and setting a 260,000-troop target. A US colonel was also announced to take a key role in German army command.

stories.headline: Pistorius leads German-Ukrainian defense industry round table to deepen arms cooperation
stories.summary: Defense Minister Pistorius hosted a round table in Berlin on April 28 with German and Ukrainian government officials and private sector representatives to discuss deepening defense industry cooperation, including joint ventures and German investment in Ukrainian arms manufacturers. Pistorius praised Ukraine's battlefield innovation and called for faster German procurement cycles drawing on Ukrainian experience.

stories.headline: AfD at record 28% in polls, ahead of CDU/CSU; 76% of Germans dissatisfied with government
stories.summary: Multiple polling institutes showed the AfD at 26–28% this week, in some surveys overtaking the CDU/CSU for the first time. Simultaneously, surveys showed 76% of Germans are dissatisfied with the CDU/CSU-SPD government and 58% believe the coalition will not survive its term. The governing coalition would no longer command a parliamentary majority based on current polling.
